epics.title: note_search empty-results investigation
epics.goal: Document why prod note_search can return empty while GET-by-id works; fix if a clear env/code bug.
epics.notes: REOPENED 2026-08-16 after the PR #8 fix failed to resolve the symptom. DIAGNOSIS UPDATED 2026-08-25 (claude-hub-session) — READ THIS BEFORE INVESTIGATING, the previous next-step in this field was wrong. (1) RULED OUT: 'check whether MINIMAX_API_KEY is set in prod' — it IS set. Verified directly against Zeabur orbita-api production env. Also present: MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.io/v1, MINIMAX_MODEL=MiniMax-M3. Do not spend another cycle on this hypothesis. (2) NOT SET in prod but harmless: EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS both have defaults in packages/lane-memory/src/config.ts ('embo-01' and 1024). MINIMAX_GROUP_ID is absent and has NO default. (3) THE REAL BLOCKER: packages/lane-memory/src/embed.ts has SIX separate `return null` paths — missing key/empty text, !response.ok, base_resp.status_code !== 0, no vector, vector.length !== EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS, and a bare catch — with ZERO logging. All six produce an identical silent null, the note is then stored with embedding=NULL, and the write reports success. So one symptom maps to five distinct root causes and the code emits no evidence of which. This is the same failure CLASS the PR #8 fix was meant to remove: that fix corrected the request protocol but kept the silence, which is why re-PUTting all 14 notes and confirming deploy freshness narrowed nothing. (4) DO THIS FIRST — instrument before fixing: make embedText emit a discriminated reason per path (HTTP status, base_resp.status_code + status_msg, actual vs expected vector length). Never log the API key or the text body. One live call then answers it outright. Fixing before instrumenting risks a third round of 'merged, still broken'. Leading candidates once instrumented: MINIMAX_GROUP_ID required and absent (the code's own comment says some MiniMax regions require it), 'embo-01' retired or wrong, or a dimension mismatch against the hardcoded 1024 default. Consider a startup assertion that an embedding round-trip works, so this fails loudly at deploy rather than silently at write time. Full write-up: personal-jacky note a21b8bf5-c253-4bb6-bee3-7f4c33c50238. BLOCKS THE HUB: until search is trustworthy, sessions resume via flat memory keys, not semantic search.

epics.title: Portfolio collectors — pull the three report lines into Orbita

epics.notes: ARCHITECTURE (decided, do not relitigate): collection lives in ORBITA, not in each product. Rationale — (1) the autopilot line is already committed to git by Maker/Checker every run; (2) the deploy line lives in Zeabur, one shared platform, one credential for all projects; (3) only the runtime line genuinely requires the app. Consequence: lines 1+2 cover every project with ZERO work in any product repo, and onboarding a new project is a registry row. CORRELATION KEY: git commit sha ties the lines together. Runtime line stays E-10 (proposed) until a product has real signals. STATUS 2026-08-29: collector code merged (T-0050..T-0053 done). epics.title: Hub activation — make the collectors actually run, and unstick the review lane
epics.goal: portfolio_brief returns real collected reports instead of 'no report ever collected', and PRs stop dying of stale locks.
epics.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-25 (claude-hub-session) after a hub session found the hub reads correctly but has never been fed. THREE STRANDS, roughly in priority order.

(1) THE GIT COLLECTOR HAS NEVER RUN. T-0051 merged 2026-08-16; nine days later portfolio_brief reports 'no report ever collected' for all seven registered projects, and note_list shows no report-type notes from any collector. The code IS wired — apps/orbita-api/src/index.ts builds portfolioSystemCollectors with portfolio_git and passes it to BOTH createHarnessRoutes and startHarnessTick. What is missing is the harness ROW: docs/personal-steward/portfolio-collectors.md names a one-time setup step, ./scripts/portfolio-git-collect-setup-harness.sh (client personal-jacky, credential github_read, template portfolio-git-collect@v1), which appears never to have been executed. Determine whether the script can be run by an agent or needs founder credentials from ~/.orbita-personal.env; if it needs the founder, say so plainly and mark needs_human rather than half-running it. THEN VERIFY BY OBSERVATION, not by exit code: call portfolio_brief and confirm at least one project's repo line is no longer stale. Also confirm private-repo reads (powerhouse, ai-business, ViOS) return real data and not a 404 recorded as an empty success.

(2) TWO PRs ARE STUCK AND THE REVIEW LANE IS FAILING A NEW WAY. T-0052 (PR #15, Zeabur collector — rebased, conflicts resolved, acceptance green) and T-0057 (PR #23, github-read tests — TS2322 fixed and pushed) were both auto-escalated to needs_human by FORCE_NEEDS_HUMAN with the SAME reason: 'lock held ~7h with task still in_review — REVIEW kept failing to complete before it could bounce the task itself'. That watchdog is a good addition, but it treats the symptom. The Checker is now STARTING review and not FINISHING it — different from the 2026-08-09 deadlock, which never started. Founder screenshots around 2026-08-16 showed the Automation intermittently Failing rather than idle. Root-cause why REVIEW does not complete (candidate: waiting on CI — PR #15 previously showed an e2e-tier-a CI FAILURE while local verify-all passed, so the review may be blocking on a check that never goes green). Merging the two PRs is worth doing on its own merits once each is re-verified, but do NOT treat merging them as closing this strand — the lane will just stall on the next PR.

(3) ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS. T-0051's acceptance was typecheck, tests, and two ripgreps — all of which passed while the feature produced nothing observable, because none of them asked whether a report was ever written. For any task whose value depends on a runtime activation step (a harness row, a feature flag, a credential, a cron), acceptance must include evidence of OUTPUT, not just of code existing. Add that as a rule wherever task-writing guidance lives in this repo, and prefer it in future tasks here.

ALSO CHECK, low priority: portfolio_brief reports kongstory and tango-atelier as enabled:true, but T-0050's own feedback says they were added as enabled:false for visibility only with no Autopilot loop. Either the registry drifted or the brief is misreporting; whichever it is, the staleness detector is currently raising findings for two projects that were never meant to report.

epics.title: Foundation hardening — tenant config, schema-sync check, resilient scheduler, docs in line with code
epics.goal: Remove hard-coded tenant identity, make schema drift detectable, make the scheduler survive crashes and multiple replicas, and bring the docs in line with the code, so the ticket work (E-16) is built on a trustworthy base.
epics.notes:
OPENED 2026-10-01 by founder decision in a hub session (claude-hub-session). Context lives in Orbita notes for client personal-jacky: decision bf7d6287-a116-49c5-8109-05f54ce34cca, design spec 6db2ffa1-a1f3-4b52-8cab-8005da730b89, repository audit d5c78787-943f-43ed-a02a-cc0a53ebd25a (read them if you have access; every fact below was verified against code on 2026-10-01 - re-verify against CODE, not docs, before relying on it). SEQUENCE: E-14 -> E-15 -> E-16 -> E-17. REPLAN rule for these four epics: decompose ONLY the first epic in that order that has no tasks yet, and only when every task of the previous epic is done (or needs_human with a recorded reason); write at most 6 small, independently mergeable tasks per REPLAN pass (contract -> logic -> API -> docs), each with machine-checkable acceptance and explicit 'do not' boundaries. PRODUCTION SAFETY RULES (apply to every task of these epics): (a) every new behaviour is behind an ORBITA_* env flag that defaults OFF, following the existing convention (explicit '0'/'1' parsing, e.g. packages/lane-platform/src/config.ts); (b) database changes are additive and idempotent only (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS); never ALTER, DROP or rename an existing table/column; runMigrations in apps/orbita-api/src/index.ts has no try/catch and runs before the server listens, so a failing migration stops production from booting; (c) the Maker/Checker loop has no Docker or Postgres - verify-all runs typecheck + pnpm test only - so tests use fakes (see packages/lane-harness/src/tick.test.ts) and SQL is protected by a text lint; real-Postgres behaviour is covered by the GitHub CI job e2e-tier-a (RUN_E2E_TIER_A=1 scripts/e2e-tier-a.sh); (d) founders-only actions must never be attempted by the Maker: flipping production flags, setting Zeabur env, creating GitHub Apps, creating credentials/API keys - write them as decisions and mark the dependent task needs_human with exact instructions; (e) never log or print secrets, API keys, private keys, installation tokens, webhook secrets or full note bodies; (f) do not modify framework-owned files (.agents/instructions/*, docs/autopilot/playbook.md, docs/autopilot/automations.md, scripts/autopilot/*), docs/autopilot/project-hooks.json (never set orbita_hub), AGENTS.md, pause-state.json, or tasks/epics outside the current epic; (g) runtime-activation acceptance rule applies: for flag-gated features, acceptance must run the code with the flag ON inside tests and must include a verify script that fails with a clear message while the feature is not activated (never call production from acceptance); (h) clients are isolated by client_id taken from the auth context only - never from request bodies - and every new query must carry a client_id predicate.

E-14 STRANDS. STRAND 1 - TENANT CONFIG. Verified hard-coded 'personal-jacky' (non-test): apps/orbita-api/src/portfolio-git-collector.ts:12 and portfolio-zeabur-collector.ts:12 (HUB_CLIENT_ID), packages/lane-oauth/src/config.ts:6 (ORBITA_MCP_OAUTH_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID default), packages/lane-portfolio/src/normalize-deploy.ts:188 (error text naming the tenant), scripts/portfolio-git-collect-setup-harness.sh, portfolio-git-collect-verify-output.sh, portfolio-zeabur-collect-setup-harness.sh, portfolio-zeabur-collect-verify-output.sh (CLIENT_ID / ORBITA_CLIENT_ID defaults and messages). Production currently depends on these defaults, so removal is TWO PHASES. Phase 1 (Maker, this epic): introduce explicit config (for example ORBITA_HUB_CLIENT_ID) read through one config module; keep the old value only as a fallback that logs a loud startup warning 'deprecated default tenant in use' so production keeps booting; scripts must take the client id from env/argument and fail with a clear message when missing (no silent default); error texts must use the configured id; tests for configured and fallback paths. Phase 2 (removing the fallback so an unset tenant fails loudly at startup) must NOT be implemented by the Maker until decision D-003 is decided (the founder first sets the env var in Zeabur). Write the Phase 2 task only after D-003 is decided; until then leave it out and record that in the epic feedback. Done-when for phase 1: a grep for the literal tenant id in non-test source finds only the documented fallback constant.

STRAND 2 - SCHEMA-SYNC CHECK. Production applies only apps/orbita-api/migrations/init.sql through runMigrations at API start; the SQL files under packages/*/drizzle are subsets and nothing verifies they agree. Add scripts/check-sql-sync.mjs (offline, no database) that parses CREATE TABLE / ADD COLUMN / CREATE INDEX statements from the lane SQL files and from init.sql and fails when a table, column or index exists in a lane file but not in init.sql. It must support an explicit allow-list file for feature-gated optional migration files (E-16 will add one) and have negative tests (a fixture with a missing column must fail). Wire it into the existing test chain via root package.json (NOT by editing the framework-owned scripts/agent-verify.sh). Do not change init.sql or existing lane SQL except to fix a mismatch the check proves; list every such fix in the task feedback; additive only.

STRAND 3 - SCHEDULER RESILIENCE (packages/lane-harness). Verified gaps: the tick has no try/catch around a run; there is no leader lock (double fire when more than one replica runs); the stored timezone is ignored by the cron next-run calculation; a crash after the run fingerprint is inserted but before completion means that slot never retries. Fix each, with unit tests using the fake db style of tick.test.ts: wrap runs so a failure never stops the tick loop; take a Postgres advisory lock for a single leader (if the lock call itself errors, continue and log a warning); honour the stored timezone when computing next runs, UTC remaining the default; record started/finished state on the fingerprint and retry a stale 'started' slot after a timeout. Keep the T-0066 semantics (next_run_at advances after every terminal outcome). Schema changes only as additive nullable columns with IF NOT EXISTS added to BOTH the lane SQL and init.sql. Do not rename or recreate the existing harness named portfolio-git-collect.

STRAND 4 - DOCS CATCH-UP (verify every statement against code). docs/product-architecture.md (harness is no longer a W27 design; add the mcp, oauth and portfolio lanes), docs/DEVELOPMENT_LANES.md and docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md (E-02, D-001 and T-0020 are done), README and connector docs (code registers 16 MCP tools; docs say 11 - list the real ones), docs/note-search-troubleshooting.md (points at the wrong package), docs/ops-multi-replica.md (state that the harness tick runs per replica until strand 3 lands). Do not create docs/project-progress.md.

BOUNDARIES: no API shape changes, no new endpoints, no changes to E-04 or E-13 tasks, no changes to the Maker/Checker scripts. ACCEPTANCE GUIDANCE: strand 1 `! rg -n 'personal-jacky' apps packages scripts --glob '!*.test.*'` with a documented allow-list for the one fallback constant; strand 2 `node scripts/check-sql-sync.mjs` exit 0 plus its negative test; strand 3 `pnpm --filter @orbita/harness test`; all tasks `./scripts/agent-verify.sh`.

epics.title: Near-real-time git sync (GitHub App webhook) feeding the portfolio reports
epics.goal: Make the hub see project git state within minutes of a push instead of once a day, and capture what the daily collector drops - open PRs including drafts, tracked non-main branches, roadmap epic statuses, lease holders and open decisions.
epics.notes:
OPENED 2026-10-01 by founder decision in a hub session (claude-hub-session). Context lives in Orbita notes for client personal-jacky: decision bf7d6287-a116-49c5-8109-05f54ce34cca, design spec 6db2ffa1-a1f3-4b52-8cab-8005da730b89, repository audit d5c78787-943f-43ed-a02a-cc0a53ebd25a (read them if you have access; every fact below was verified against code on 2026-10-01 - re-verify against CODE, not docs, before relying on it). SEQUENCE: E-14 -> E-15 -> E-16 -> E-17. REPLAN rule for these four epics: decompose ONLY the first epic in that order that has no tasks yet, and only when every task of the previous epic is done (or needs_human with a recorded reason); write at most 6 small, independently mergeable tasks per REPLAN pass (contract -> logic -> API -> docs), each with machine-checkable acceptance and explicit 'do not' boundaries. PRODUCTION SAFETY RULES (apply to every task of these epics): (a) every new behaviour is behind an ORBITA_* env flag that defaults OFF, following the existing convention (explicit '0'/'1' parsing, e.g. packages/lane-platform/src/config.ts); (b) database changes are additive and idempotent only (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS); never ALTER, DROP or rename an existing table/column; runMigrations in apps/orbita-api/src/index.ts has no try/catch and runs before the server listens, so a failing migration stops production from booting; (c) the Maker/Checker loop has no Docker or Postgres - verify-all runs typecheck + pnpm test only - so tests use fakes (see packages/lane-harness/src/tick.test.ts) and SQL is protected by a text lint; real-Postgres behaviour is covered by the GitHub CI job e2e-tier-a (RUN_E2E_TIER_A=1 scripts/e2e-tier-a.sh); (d) founders-only actions must never be attempted by the Maker: flipping production flags, setting Zeabur env, creating GitHub Apps, creating credentials/API keys - write them as decisions and mark the dependent task needs_human with exact instructions; (e) never log or print secrets, API keys, private keys, installation tokens, webhook secrets or full note bodies; (f) do not modify framework-owned files (.agents/instructions/*, docs/autopilot/playbook.md, docs/autopilot/automations.md, scripts/autopilot/*), docs/autopilot/project-hooks.json (never set orbita_hub), AGENTS.md, pause-state.json, or tasks/epics outside the current epic; (g) runtime-activation acceptance rule applies: for flag-gated features, acceptance must run the code with the flag ON inside tests and must include a verify script that fails with a clear message while the feature is not activated (never call production from acceptance); (h) clients are isolated by client_id taken from the auth context only - never from request bodies - and every new query must carry a client_id predicate.

E-15 CONTEXT. The daily collector (06:00 UTC) reads only the default branch (backlog, roadmap, locks, pause-state, commits) and discards PRs, other branches, roadmap epics and lock holders; the founder's working conversations revolve around current progress, so a day-old picture is too stale. Founder chose a GitHub App (read-only Contents + Push event) over per-repo webhooks. DESIGN (agreed): GitHub App -> signed webhook POST /v1/inbound/github -> verify -> debounce -> read docs/autopilot/*.json at the pushed sha with a short-lived installation token -> write the EXISTING report note shape (type report, edge repo, stable note id per project, provenance measured, include git sha and synced_at) so portfolio_brief benefits immediately. A reconcile job compares each registered repo's head sha with the last synced sha and re-syncs on difference (webhooks can be missed). The existing daily portfolio_git collector stays exactly as it is until the new pipeline is proven - do not remove or alter it in this epic.

REQUIREMENTS. (1) Secrets: the webhook secret and the App private key live in the credentials vault (write-once POST /v1/admin/credentials; there is no update route, so rotation means a new credential name with a version suffix - document it). Resolve them with resolveCredentialSecret like the collectors do, NOT from env tokens like /v1/inbound/email. Never log secrets, private keys, installation tokens or payload bodies. (2) Receiver: raw-body HMAC-SHA256 verification of X-Hub-Signature-256 with constant-time comparison; 401 without revealing why; body size limit; X-GitHub-Delivery de-duplication (idempotent); accept only push events (ping returns 200); ignore repositories that are not in the portfolio registry and pushes touching no docs/autopilot/** path; respond fast (202) and process asynchronously with retry. (3) App auth module: RS256 JWT from the private key using Node crypto only (no new heavy dependency), exchange for an installation token, cache until shortly before expiry, never persist tokens; READ-ONLY - the code must not call any GitHub write endpoint (test that asserts only GET requests are issued). (4) Tracked refs: default branch plus an optional per-project list of tracked branches in docs/personal-steward/portfolio-registry.json (the book repository works on a long-lived integration branch). (5) Extend the repo report with open PRs (number, title, draft, head branch, T-id if any), tracked branch heads, roadmap epic statuses, lock holders (task, by, since, pr) and open decisions; keep docs/autopilot/report.schema.json validity - add sections rather than changing schema_version unless unavoidable. (6) Reconcile job every N minutes (configurable, default 15) with unit tests. Do NOT add MCP tools in this epic. (7) Everything behind ORBITA_GITHUB_APP_ENABLED (default OFF): with the flag off the route returns 404 and the reconcile job does not run.

FOUNDER-ONLY STEPS (decision D-004, default_if_silent null): create the GitHub App (Contents: read-only, event Push, installed on the registry repositories), store webhook secret + private key + App id + installation id in the vault via the admin API, flip the flag in Zeabur. The Maker must NOT attempt any of this; the final activation task must be status needs_human with exact step-by-step instructions until D-004 is decided.

ACCEPTANCE GUIDANCE: unit tests with signed fixture payloads (valid, bad signature, replay, ignored repo, irrelevant path); JWT unit test with a keypair generated inside the test; report-shape test validated against docs/autopilot/report.schema.json; scripts/github-sync-verify-output.sh modelled on scripts/portfolio-git-collect-verify-output.sh that exits non-zero with a clear message when the flag/credentials are absent (never run against production in acceptance); ./scripts/agent-verify.sh. BOUNDARIES: no write access to GitHub; no change to the existing portfolio_git collector behaviour; no change to project-hooks.json; never add orbita_hub.

epics.goal: A ticket system for non-code and code work that several agents can read, claim and update safely: separate tables, a verb-based API distinct from notes, append-only event history, atomic claim with lease, deterministic queries.

IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS); never ALTER, DROP or rename an existing table/column; runMigrations in apps/orbita-api/src/index.ts has no try/catch and runs before the server listens, so a failing migration stops production from booting; (c) the Maker/Checker loop has no Docker or Postgres - verify-all runs typecheck + pnpm test only - so tests use fakes (see packages/lane-harness/src/tick.test.ts) and SQL is protected by a text lint; real-Postgres behaviour is covered by the GitHub CI job e2e-tier-a (RUN_E2E_TIER_A=1 scripts/e2e-tier-a.sh); (d) founders-only actions must never be attempted by the Maker: flipping production flags, setting Zeabur env, creating GitHub Apps, creating credentials/API keys - write them as decisions and mark the dependent task needs_human with exact instructions; (e) never log or print secrets, API keys, private keys, installation tokens, webhook secrets or full note bodies; (f) do not modify framework-owned files (.agents/instructions/*, docs/autopilot/playbook.md, docs/autopilot/automations.md, scripts/autopilot/*), docs/autopilot/project-hooks.json (never set orbita_hub), AGENTS.md, pause-state.json, or tasks/epics outside the current epic; (g) runtime-activation acceptance rule applies: for flag-gated features, acceptance must run the code with the flag ON inside tests and must include a verify script that fails with a clear message while the feature is not activated (never call production from acceptance); (h) clients are isolated by client_id taken from the auth context only - never from request bodies - and every new query must carry a client_id predicate.

E-16 DESIGN (agreed; see spec 6db2ffa1). Tickets are NOT notes: notes have no atomic claim, no versioning, no event history, MCP note_list has no filters and note_search can silently return empty. Build a new package packages/lane-tickets following the repo's lane rules: INTERFACE.md FIRST, then contracts, then logic; the first task of this epic must contain only INTERFACE.md plus JSON-Schema contracts (states, transitions, verbs, request/response shapes) under packages/lane-tickets/contracts/ with a validity test; add .agents/skills/lane-tickets/SKILL.md and a simulator fixture; never import another lane's src.

TASK ORDER: (1) INTERFACE.md + contracts; (2) pure state-machine module with an exhaustive (state x verb) table test; (3) repository layer behind an interface with a fake implementation used by tests; (4) REST routes /v1/tickets (separate namespace from notes) with openapi entries; (5) additive MCP tools (tool names ticket_*; adding tools is additive - do not change existing tool contracts); (6) docs + feature-gated migration + tier-A test.

DATA MODEL (additive, idempotent). Table tickets: id uuid, client_id, project, function (dev|infra|support|marketing|sales|ops|research), kind (work|decision), title, description, status, owner (human | claude | agent:<name>), requester, priority, next_action, blocked_on, risk_tier (L0|L1|L2|money), source (native|git), source_ref, git_ref, synced_at, sync_state (confirmed|pending-sync|drift) , version int, lease_holder, lease_expires_at, idempotency_key, data jsonb (free extension), created_at, updated_at. Table ticket_events: append-only (no update or delete code path exists): id, ticket_id, client_id, seq, actor, verb, from_status, to_status, payload jsonb, at. States: proposed -> approved -> claimed -> in_progress -> in_review -> done; side states waiting_human, blocked, cancelled. proposed->approved and cancel of a proposed ticket are HUMAN approvals; an expired lease automatically returns the ticket to approved with an event.

VERBS (not CRUD): ticket_create, ticket_list, ticket_get, ticket_approve, ticket_claim (atomic, with lease: single UPDATE ... WHERE status='approved' AND lease free/expired RETURNING, or SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), ticket_extend, ticket_progress, ticket_complete (requires at least one result link/reference), ticket_block, ticket_request_decision, ticket_comment, ticket_cancel. Optimistic concurrency via expected_version; idempotency keys unique per (client_id, verb, key); structured deterministic list queries (project, function, status, owner, updated_since, cursor pagination, hard limit) that never load the whole table into memory. Tickets with source=git are READ-ONLY here: any transition returns 409 with a pointer to the git file (the git mirror is a later epic; native tickets only now). Until E-17 provides principals, approve/cancel-of-proposed is allowed only for API keys listed in ORBITA_TICKETS_APPROVER_KEY_IDS (default empty = nobody can approve).

TENANCY: client_id from the auth context only; every query has a client_id predicate; tests with two clients must prove isolation.

PRODUCTION SAFETY: ALL ticket DDL lives in a SEPARATE optional migration file applied only when ORBITA_TICKETS_ENABLED=1 (default OFF). Flag off = DDL is not run, routes and MCP tools are not mounted, behaviour of the running system is unchanged. DDL: IF NOT EXISTS only, never touching existing tables; the DDL PR must include a pure-text SQL lint test (no DROP, no ALTER of existing tables) and a tier-A test (runs with the flag ON, applies the DDL twice) executed by the GitHub CI job e2e-tier-a. Register the optional file in the E-14 check-sql-sync allow-list (if E-14's check does not exist yet, create the allow-list entry in the same task and note it). Flipping ORBITA_TICKETS_ENABLED in production is the founder's decision D-005 (default_if_silent null) with a pre-flip checklist: e2e-tier-a green with the flag on, DDL run on a scratch database.

DO NOT: modify the notes API, notes tables or note_* MCP tools; touch any existing table; call an LLM; build any UI; implement the git mirror, workflows or a bot integration; add per-agent identity (E-17). ACCEPTANCE GUIDANCE: package tests, contract validity test, state-machine table test, tenant-isolation test, DDL lint test, route/openapi presence test, golden test proving that with the flag off the MCP tool list and route table are byte-identical to before; ./scripts/agent-verify.sh.

epics.title: Agent identity and tool-level permissions (shadow mode first)
epics.goal: Know which agent did what and restrict what each agent may do - the prerequisite for letting an external agent, for example a bot that browses untrusted web pages, anywhere near the hub.
epics.notes:
OPENED 2026-10-01 by founder decision in a hub session (claude-hub-session). Context lives in Orbita notes for client personal-jacky: decision bf7d6287-a116-49c5-8109-05f54ce34cca, design spec 6db2ffa1-a1f3-4b52-8cab-8005da730b89, repository audit d5c78787-943f-43ed-a02a-cc0a53ebd25a (read them if you have access; every fact below was verified against code on 2026-10-01 - re-verify against CODE, not docs, before relying on it). SEQUENCE: E-14 -> E-15 -> E-16 -> E-17. REPLAN rule for these four epics: decompose ONLY the first epic in that order that has no tasks yet, and only when every task of the previous epic is done (or needs_human with a recorded reason); write at most 6 small, independently mergeable tasks per REPLAN pass (contract -> logic -> API -> docs), each with machine-checkable acceptance and explicit 'do not' boundaries. PRODUCTION SAFETY RULES (apply to every task of these epics): (a) every new behaviour is behind an ORBITA_* env flag that defaults OFF, following the existing convention (explicit '0'/'1' parsing, e.g. packages/lane-platform/src/config.ts); (b) database changes are additive and idempotent only (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS); never ALTER, DROP or rename an existing table/column; runMigrations in apps/orbita-api/src/index.ts has no try/catch and runs before the server listens, so a failing migration stops production from booting; (c) the Maker/Checker loop has no Docker or Postgres - verify-all runs typecheck + pnpm test only - so tests use fakes (see packages/lane-harness/src/tick.test.ts) and SQL is protected by a text lint; real-Postgres behaviour is covered by the GitHub CI job e2e-tier-a (RUN_E2E_TIER_A=1 scripts/e2e-tier-a.sh); (d) founders-only actions must never be attempted by the Maker: flipping production flags, setting Zeabur env, creating GitHub Apps, creating credentials/API keys - write them as decisions and mark the dependent task needs_human with exact instructions; (e) never log or print secrets, API keys, private keys, installation tokens, webhook secrets or full note bodies; (f) do not modify framework-owned files (.agents/instructions/*, docs/autopilot/playbook.md, docs/autopilot/automations.md, scripts/autopilot/*), docs/autopilot/project-hooks.json (never set orbita_hub), AGENTS.md, pause-state.json, or tasks/epics outside the current epic; (g) runtime-activation acceptance rule applies: for flag-gated features, acceptance must run the code with the flag ON inside tests and must include a verify script that fails with a clear message while the feature is not activated (never call production from acceptance); (h) clients are isolated by client_id taken from the auth context only - never from request bodies - and every new query must carry a client_id predicate.

E-17 CONTEXT. Today OAuth/MCP scopes are only sessions:create and sessions:use; any caller that passes gets all 16 MCP tools, including note_put, github_get_file/list_commits/list_pull_requests and trigger_automation, and cannot be told apart from another caller (one API key maps to one client_id). A browsing agent that reads hostile web content while holding those rights is a prompt-injection hazard; so identity and tool-level scopes must exist BEFORE any external agent is connected.

DESIGN. Additive tables (created only when ORBITA_AGENT_PRINCIPALS_ENABLED=1, default OFF, same optional-migration pattern as E-16): agent_principals (id, client_id, name, kind: human|claude|cursor|external-agent|internal-worker, bound API key id, scopes text[], status, created_at), agent_audit (append-only: principal, tool/route, decision allow|deny|would-deny, at, short reason; no payload bodies). Scope vocabulary: tickets:read, tickets:claim, tickets:write:<function>, tickets:approve, notes:read, notes:write, github:read, automation:trigger, admin, plus the legacy sessions:use. Every MCP tool declares its required scope in one table; a test must FAIL if any registered tool has no mapping, so a new tool cannot be added without a scope. Rollout mode ORBITA_AGENT_SCOPES_MODE = off | shadow | enforce (default off): shadow evaluates permissions and writes would-deny rows without blocking anything; enforce blocks. LEGACY: every existing API key and OAuth session maps to a built-in principal 'legacy-full' holding all scopes, so nothing breaks; principals created later default to least privilege. OAuth dynamic-client consent maps to a principal. Admin routes (existing admin token) create/list/revoke principals and bind keys; no secret is ever returned. If E-16 exists, add the ticket scopes and make tickets:approve replace the ORBITA_TICKETS_APPROVER_KEY_IDS fallback (keep the fallback working when mode is off).

FOUNDER-ONLY (decision D-006, default_if_silent null): switching the mode from shadow to enforce in production and creating principals for real agents (for example a Grok Bot with a dedicated brand account) - the Maker must not do either.

DO NOT: change the API key format or break existing keys; remove sessions:use; change credential-vault semantics; integrate any external agent; touch note storage. ACCEPTANCE GUIDANCE: permission-matrix unit tests (every MCP tool x principal kind), shadow versus enforce behaviour, legacy principal, audit rows, tool-without-scope test, and a golden test proving that with mode=off the tools/list output and a sample call are unchanged; ./scripts/agent-verify.sh.
